grader_prompt: You are evaluating whether a stackhawk-data-seed skill run was orchestrated correctly. This skill is a thin CLI-driving stub: it drives `hawk perch seed --events json` and relays the command's JSONL phase events. The seed methodology (discovery, manifest synthesis, idempotency) lives INSIDE the hawk CLI — the agent's job is orchestration, not authoring. Review the agent's output text and command history (preflight checks, the `hawk perch seed` invocation, how it relayed phase events, the final handoff) and any files under data-seed/ that the CLI produced. Do NOT penalize the agent for not hand-writing discovery logic or a manifest — that is correct. For each check below, determine pass/fail and write a one-sentence explanation. Return a JSON object conforming to rubric-schema.json.

checks.description: The agent ran the preflight: confirmed it is in a git repo, and confirmed `hawk perch seed` is available (e.g. `hawk perch seed --help`). If the command was unavailable it punted with an upgrade instruction rather than hand-authoring seed data.
The agent invoked `hawk perch seed --events json` (with an --app-host the user supplied or was asked for) as the seeding mechanism, rather than reimplementing discovery/synthesis itself.
checks.focus: The hawk perch seed invocation in the command history

checks.description: The agent consumed the JSONL phase events (starting/extracting/synthesizing/validating/finalizing/done) and surfaced concise, accurate progress to the user, and acted on any review prompt or non-zero exit instead of ignoring it.
checks.focus: How agent output tracks the emitted phase events

checks.description: The agent did NOT hand-author seed artifacts — no manual storage-signal greps (Liquibase/Flyway/Prisma/etc.) and no hand-written data-seed/manifest.yaml or per-service seed scripts. Any artifacts under data-seed/ were produced by the CLI, not typed by the agent.
checks.focus: Command history for manual discovery/authoring vs. delegation to the CLI

checks.description: The agent reported the run's actual outcome honestly. In particular, if the run reported no local storage / nothing to seed (e.g. a gateway with storageKind NONE), it relayed that no-op result rather than fabricating fake entities to appear productive.
checks.focus: Agent's interpretation of the run result, especially the empty/no-op case

checks.description: The agent did not create or modify stackhawk.yml (hawkscan's domain) and did not start the application stack (docker-compose up / bootRun / npm start). The handoff to hawkscan is via .data-seed-credentials.env only.
checks.focus: stackhawk.yml absence/unchanged and absence of app-startup commands

checks.description: On success the agent clearly reported what the CLI wrote (data-seed/ + manifest.yaml + .data-seed-credentials.env), the next steps (review, replay, run hawkscan), and that hawkscan reads .data-seed-credentials.env. Reminded the user the credentials file is gitignored and must not be committed.
